title: Re-Volt/Gameplay
text:
Your goal in this game is to complete a number of laps by finishing in the top 3 place. Every successfully won race will allow you to unlock new cars and tracks for you to use.

Menu screen

The game has 6 options in the main menu:

 Start Race: See all the modes and difficulties of the game from which you can choose to start playing the game and how many cars and tracks you have unlocked. If there is no progress yet, then only the first four tracks and first class of cars will be available to play for now. In Car Selection is shown which car and track you want to choose for racing.
 Best Trial Times: See who completed races fastest.
 Progress Table: See how many races you have won, how many cups you have won, and how many stars in Stunt Arena you have collected.
 Options: To modify music, sound, controls, resolution, graphics, and desired number of laps and cars for Single Race.
 Track Editor: Create your own custom tracks.
 Quit: Exit the game.

Modes

There are 6 modes available:

 Single Race: Normal mode where you are simply racing.
 Championship: Competitive mode where you must place on 3rd or higher place to compete further and win to unlock new cars and tracks.
 Multi-Player: Mode where you can either play normal race with real-life people, or Battle Tag where you must find, collect, and hold the star until the time runs out.
 Time Trial: Mode where you must surprass current best time of any track
 Practice: Mode where you must find and collect Secret Star hidden on every track, and where you can practice your driving skills
 Stunt Arena: Mode where you must find and collect twenty Secret Stars to unlock Clockwork Carnage mode, and where you can practice driving stunts.
 Clockwork Carnage': Mode that is same as Single Race, except all cars are clockwork cars.

Difficulties

On the "Junior RC" aka Easy difficulty, collisions with opposing cars are simple, but all cars travel at reduced speed for some degree. Many newcomers will find it difficult to control most cars in the game due to their nimble and fast characteristics. Therefore, Junior RC is here to slow down pace of the game to make it enticing for new players, making it perfect mode for family or friends. On the "Console" aka Medium difficulty, collisions with opposing cars are simple, and all cars travel at full speed. Console difficulty is very forgiving in terms of errors, because colliding against walls only causes the vehicle to lose speed but allows control to be retained, making it suitable for new players wanting to try full speed of cars in the game while being lenient on mistakes and crashes they make. On the "Arcade" aka Hard difficulty, collisions with opposing cars are simple yet complex, and all cars travel at full speed. In Arcade, cars can still easily retain control should they collide with each other, and simple car physics simply cause racers to lose speed upon collision. While playing on Arcade, you must be wary of crashing into walls because they will have major disruption on cars. On the "Simulation" aka Insane difficulty, collisions with opposing cars are realistic, and all cars travel at full speed. In Simulation, complex physics will cause you to lose both speed and control if you crash either into cars or walls. Notion of avoiding contact with opposing racers makes Simulation mode especially challenging because cars can drive on top of each other, thereby losing control for cars caught in the incident.

Interface
thumb|Re-Volt's ingame interface
At the top on the left side of the screen is shown how many laps you have completed, how many laps you have left to complete, and icon of Power-Up that you will receive after you collect Pick Up. At the top on the right side of the screen is shown what is your best time for last lap that you have completed, what is your best time for single lap of track, how much time has passed during lap, and how much time has passed during entire race. At the bottom on the left side of the screen is shown what is your current position in the race and how far ahead and behind are racer one place before and after you, and arrow that shows in which direction you are currently driving. At the bottom on the right side of the screen is speedometer that shows how fast you are driving. Arrow that will show direction in which you must proceed in the race will occasionally appear to help you determine where you must go to avoid getting lost, or letter X that will blink if you are going in the wrong direction. Arrow that shows direction can appear either at the botton on the left side of the screen, or in the middle at the top of the screen, depending on your game version.

Scoring

Each time you finish race either first, or second, or third, you will score points that will place you in higher position in Championship mode.
